issues.description: Problem statement requires the function 'start_app' to be the global entry point, but the template exposes 'main' as the global symbol (global main / main:). The provided solution also declares 'global main' while defining a non-global 'start_app' label. This mismatch (expected global start_app vs. template/solution using global main or an unexported start_app) will confuse students about which symbol they must implement and may prevent the exercise harness from recognizing the correct entry point.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the entry-point symbol consistent with the problem statement. For example, in the template replace or augment 'global main' with 'global start_app' and ensure a 'start_app:' label is present (or rename the existing 'main:' label to 'start_app:'). Similarly, update the solution to declare 'global start_app' (instead of or in addition to 'global main') so that the global entry point is unambiguously 'start_app'. This preserves the pedagogical intent while removing the naming/visibility mismatch.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires the function start_app to be the global entry point, but the template declares and exposes main (global main / main:) rather than start_app. The solution contains a start_app label but does not declare it global (it still declares global main), so across artifacts the intended entry-point identifier is referenced inconsistently. This creates a mapping barrier: students are told to provide a global start_app but the starter code uses main and the reference solution fails to mark start_app as global, making it unclear which symbol must be exported as the program entry point.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the entry-point identifier consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred): change the template to declare and use start_app as the global entry point — replace 'global main' with 'global start_app' and rename the 'main:' label to 'start_app:'. Update the solution to also declare 'global start_app' (or remove/rename the separate 'main' symbol) so the solution matches the problem requirement. Option B: if 'main' is the intended exported symbol, update the problem statement to require 'main' instead of 'start_app'. Ensure only one canonical global entry label is used in template and solution to avoid student confusion.
